Muhammad of Ghor.question: Hariraja, briefly dislodged the Ghurid garrison from Ajmer, but was later defeated by Qutb ud-_____
Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Hariraja, briefly dislodged the Ghurid garrison from Ajmer, but was later defeated by Qutb ud-Din Aibak. Delhi was also captured by Muhammad and Qutb al-Din Aibak in 1193, although in continuation with the policy adopted earlier in Ajmer, a puppet Rajput scion was installed in Delhi in return for tribute (possibly the son of Govindraja who died in Tarain).

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Muhammad continued to carry out raids across the north Indian plain. Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: However, he later became preoccupied with the Ghurid expansion in Transoxiana against the Khwarezmian Empire as his brother Ghiyath al-Din began to have health problems.

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Muhammad of Ghor.question: According to Fakhr-i _____ and Minhaj-i Siraj Juzjani, Muhammad appointed Aibak as his administrator of the Ghurid domains in North India after the Second Battle of Tarain
Muhammad of Ghor.fact: According to Fakhr-i Mudabbir and Minhaj-i Siraj Juzjani, Muhammad appointed Aibak as his administrator of the Ghurid domains in North India after the Second Battle of Tarain.

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Accordingly, in 1194, he crossed the Jamuna River with an army of 50,000 horsemen where he confronted the forces of the Rajput Gahadavala king Jayachandra in the Battle of Chandawar.

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: The Gahadavala capital Kanauj was annexed in 1198.

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: During this campaign, the Buddhist city of Sarnath was also sacked.

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Muhammad, along with Qutb ud-Din Aibak, advanced and besieged Thankar whose ruler Kumarpal was defeated.

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Muhammad placed the fort under his senior slave Bahauddin Tughril, who later set up Sultankot and used it as his stronghold.

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Muhammad, along with Qutb ud-Din Aibak, advanced and besieged Thankar whose ruler Kumarpal was defeated. Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Muhammad placed the fort under his senior slave Bahauddin Tughril, who later set up Sultankot and used it as his stronghold. After the assassination of Muhammad, Tughril styled himself as the Sultan in Bayana.

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Muhammad of Ghor.question: In _____, Qutb ud-Din Aibak invaded Gujarat and defeated Bhima II in Sirohi after a sudden attack and afterwards sacked his capital Anhilwara
Muhammad of Ghor.fact: In 1197, Qutb ud-Din Aibak invaded Gujarat and defeated Bhima II in Sirohi after a sudden attack and afterwards sacked his capital Anhilwara.

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
Muhammad of Ghor.question: Thus, Aibak avenged the rout of Muhammad at the same place in _____

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Thus, taking advantage of his absence from Herat where he had appointed his nephew Alp Ghazi to be in charge, Khwarezmian forces captured Merv and beheaded the Ghurid governor Karang.

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: According to Juzjani, the negotiations between Muhammad and Taniku were arranged by Uthman ibn Ibrahim of Samarkand who did not want the "Sultan of Islam" to be captured by "the infidels".

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Following the defeat, the Ghurids lost the control over most of the Khurasan except Herat and Balkh.

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Thus, Muhammad of necessity agreed a peace with the Khwarezmians.

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: Ibn al-Athir further supports this and states that most of the Indians had followed them and 'cast off obedience' to the Ghorid emir of Lahore also plundering Lahore.

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: He then turned his attention towards Central Asia to avenge the rout at Andhkhud and to reclaim his holdings in Khurasan.

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.fact: He describes the assassination in great detail and narrates that 'a body of infidel Khokhars dogged his army determined to slay him because of the killing and taking of prisoners and captives he had inflicted on them' and that they dealt twenty four wounds to the sultan. Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins

Muhammad of Ghor.subject: Indian Handicrafts & Coins
